chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn Ayyub from Ali ibn Asbat from Al-Hakam ibn Miskin from Yusuf ibn Suhayb from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) turned towards Abu Bakr in the cave and said to him, 'Be still, for Allah is with us.' And tremor had seized him, and he was not still. So when the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saw his state, he said to him, 'Do you want me to show you my companions from the Ansar in their gatherings talking? And I will show you Ja'far and his companions in the sea diving?' He said, 'Yes.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) wiped his hand over his face, and he looked at the Ansar talking, and he looked at Ja'far (peace be upon him) and his companions in the sea diving. So he mentally affirmed at that moment that he was a sorcerer.

key_terms.أَضْمَرَ: He affirmed mentally / He kept it secret in his heart
key_terms.الْأَنْصَارِ: The Helpers (companions of the Prophet from Medina)
key_terms.الْغَارِ: The Cave (often referring to the Cave of Thawr)

ai.seo_question: What did Abu Bakr think when the Prophet showed him Ja'far ibn Abi Talib diving in the sea?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) reveals the spiritual station of Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) and his companions diving in the sea, contrasting their deep spiritual immersion with the Ansar's worldly discussions. This miraculous display serves as a subtle indicator of Ja'far's elevated status, prompting Abu Bakr to internally label the Prophet a sorcerer, a reaction often interpreted in Shia scholarship as a precursor to his eventual selection or a reflection of his limited spiritual perception. The event underscores the Shia emphasis on the esoteric knowledge and divine favor bestowed upon the Ahl al-Bayt.
